# Section 2.1 — Binary inference and credible-set calibration

**Concept.** Beta conjugacy converts successes and failures into updated shape
parameters. A posterior density supports several point summaries
and credible intervals.

**Example.** A laboratory observes seven passes in twenty trials.
A `Beta(2,8)` prior gives a `Beta(9,21)` posterior.

Compute the posterior summaries and an equal-tailed interval. For the
shortest interval, optimize where to put the lower endpoint while
holding posterior mass fixed at 95%.

```{r s21-beta-update}
s21_a0 <- 2; s21_b0 <- 8; s21_n <- 20; s21_passes <- 7
s21_an <- s21_a0+s21_passes
s21_bn <- s21_b0+s21_n-s21_passes
c(mean=s21_an/(s21_an+s21_bn),
 median=qbeta(.5,s21_an,s21_bn),
 mode=(s21_an-1)/(s21_an+s21_bn-2),
 asymmetric_loss_action=qbeta(.8,s21_an,s21_bn))
s21_equal_tail <- qbeta(c(.025,.975),s21_an,s21_bn)
# Shortest 95% interval for this unimodal density.
s21_width <- function(u) diff(qbeta(c(u,u+.95),s21_an,s21_bn))
s21_lower_mass <- optimize(s21_width,c(0,.05))$minimum
s21_hpd <- qbeta(c(s21_lower_mass,s21_lower_mass+.95),s21_an,s21_bn)
rbind(equal_tail=s21_equal_tail, HPD=s21_hpd)
stopifnot(abs(diff(pbeta(s21_hpd,s21_an,s21_bn))-.95)<1e-10)
```

```{r s21-lecture-update, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Lecture notes, Section 2.1. Panel A shows the update calculated above."}
notes_figure("section2-beta-update.png")
```

## Credible-set calibration

**Concept.** Coverage at a fixed true rate averages over repeated
samples. Prior average coverage also averages over the rate.

**Example.** Use ten trials and a uniform prior. There are eleven
possible reported 90% equal-tailed intervals.

Find the interval for each possible count. At any true rate, sum the
binomial probabilities of the counts whose intervals contain it.

```{r s21-coverage}
s21_s <- 0:10
s21_lo <- qbeta(.05,s21_s+1,11-s21_s)
s21_hi <- qbeta(.95,s21_s+1,11-s21_s)
s21_coverage <- function(theta) sum(dbinom(s21_s,10,theta)*
                                      (s21_lo<=theta & theta<=s21_hi))
s21_average <- sum((pbeta(s21_hi,s21_s+1,11-s21_s)-
                    pbeta(s21_lo,s21_s+1,11-s21_s))/11)
c(at_0.1=s21_coverage(.1),at_0.5=s21_coverage(.5),prior_average=s21_average)
stopifnot(abs(s21_average-.9)<1e-12)
```

```{r s21-lecture-coverage, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Lecture notes, Section 2.1. Coverage changes with the true rate even though its prior average is 0.90."}
notes_figure("section12-coverage.png")
```

Posterior probability and fixed-parameter coverage answer different
questions. **Extension:** repeat this calculation under `Beta(2,8)` and
verify the average using that prior, rather than a uniform average.

# Section 2.2 — Incident rates, exposure, and prediction

**Concept.** Counts update the Gamma shape and total exposure updates the rate.
A future count mixes Poisson probabilities over the updated Gamma law.

**Example.** Observe eight daily incident counts, each with one day of
exposure. Use a Gamma prior with shape and **rate** both equal to 2.

Add the total count and exposure to the prior parameters. Convert the
updated rate and future exposure to the success probability used by
R's negative-binomial distribution.

```{r s22-poisson}
s22_counts <- c(1,0,3,2,1,4,2,3)
knitr::kable(data.frame(day=1:8,incidents=s22_counts,exposure_days=1))
s22_a0 <- 2; s22_b0 <- 2
s22_an <- s22_a0+sum(s22_counts)
s22_bn <- s22_b0+length(s22_counts)
s22_future_exposure <- 1
s22_prob <- s22_bn/(s22_bn+s22_future_exposure)
c(posterior_mean=s22_an/s22_bn,
 posterior_variance=s22_an/s22_bn^2,
 predictive_mean=s22_future_exposure*s22_an/s22_bn,
 predictive_variance=s22_future_exposure*s22_an/s22_bn+
   s22_future_exposure^2*s22_an/s22_bn^2,
 zero_probability=dnbinom(0,size=s22_an,prob=s22_prob))
stopifnot(s22_an==18,s22_bn==10,
 abs(dnbinom(0,size=s22_an,prob=s22_prob)-(10/11)^18)<1e-12)
```

The lecture figure uses ten future days to make the additional variance
visible. Compute both predictive variances at the same expected count.

```{r s22-ten-day}
s22_ten_days <- 10
s22_mean_ten <- s22_ten_days * s22_an / s22_bn
s22_rate_uncertainty <- s22_ten_days^2 * s22_an / s22_bn^2
c(mean = s22_mean_ten, plug_in_variance = s22_mean_ten,
  predictive_variance = s22_mean_ten + s22_rate_uncertainty)
```

```{r s22-lecture-prediction, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Lecture notes, Section 2.2. Both ten-day forecasts have mean 18."}
notes_figure("audit26-poisson-prediction.png")
```

The future count includes both Poisson variation and uncertain-rate
variation. **Extension:** convert all exposures to hours. The hourly rate
is the daily rate divided by 24; multiply the Gamma rate hyperparameters
by 24 and verify unchanged prediction for one physical day.

# Section 2.3 — Additive information in a natural conjugate family

**Concept.** In a natural conjugate update, the sample adds sufficient
statistics and sample size to the prior information coordinates.

**Example.** Observe `(0,1,2)` with unit sampling variance and a normal
prior centered at one with precision two.

Add three units of precision and the sum of the observations. To check
the evidence, compare direct numerical integration with the ratio of
conjugate normalizers multiplied by the data's base-density term.

```{r s23-natural-update}
s23_x <- c(0,1,2)
s23_k0 <- 2; s23_m0 <- 1
s23_kn <- s23_k0+length(s23_x)
s23_mn <- (s23_k0*s23_m0+sum(s23_x))/s23_kn
c(posterior_mean=s23_mn,posterior_variance=1/s23_kn)
# Integrate the normalized likelihood times prior to check evidence.
s23_evidence <- integrate(function(mu) dnorm(mu,s23_m0,sqrt(1/s23_k0))*
 exp(vapply(mu,function(m)sum(dnorm(s23_x,m,1,log=TRUE)),0.)),
 -Inf,Inf)$value
s23_logZ <- function(k,m) .5*log(2*pi/k)+k*m^2/2
s23_logh <- sum(dnorm(s23_x,0,1,log=TRUE))
s23_formula <- exp(s23_logh+s23_logZ(s23_kn,s23_mn)-
                    s23_logZ(s23_k0,s23_m0))
c(numerical_evidence=s23_evidence,normalizer_ratio=s23_formula)
stopifnot(abs(s23_mn-1)<1e-12,
 abs(s23_evidence-s23_formula)<1e-9)
```

```{r s23-density-visual}
s23_mu <- seq(-1.5, 3.5, length.out = 401)
s23_prior <- dnorm(s23_mu, s23_m0, 1 / sqrt(s23_k0))
s23_posterior <- dnorm(s23_mu, s23_mn, 1 / sqrt(s23_kn))
plot(s23_mu, s23_posterior, type = "l", col = "#0072B2", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Mean", ylab = "Density")
lines(s23_mu, s23_prior, col = "grey35", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
legend("topright", c("Posterior", "Prior"), col = c("#0072B2", "grey35"),
       lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
```

The evidence needs the base-density terms as well as the normalizer
ratio. **Extension:** update sequentially with `(0)` and then `(1,2)`;
reverse the batches and verify the same final information coordinates.
